before_copy.tools/README.md (line 844 before this st: Servers for the page specs: a spec starts the server it needs with `startStand` or `withStand` from `test/e2e/kit/index.js`. The server is a Node program started with an argument list; it gets a short list of environment variables (`PATH`, `TMPDIR`, `TEMP`, `TMP`, `LANG`, `LC_ALL`, `TZ`, `SystemRoot`), a home folder of its own (`HOME` and `USERPROFILE` point to a new folder under the temporary root, so Node's `os.homedir()` in the server gives that folder, never the home folder of the person; the spec cannot give these two) and what the spec gives, nothing else; the system and Node may add variables of their own, none of them given by the starter (`__CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING` on macOS, and `NODE_V8_COVERAGE` when the spec process has it). A state folder reaches the server only through `stateEnv` (pairs of a variable and a folder) or as an argument; every folder of `stateEnv`, every value of `env` and every argument that is an absolute path, or holds one after `=`, must lie under the temporary root (not the root itself) and outside the repository, else nothing is started (`PATH_REFUSED`); the first argument, the script, may also be a path inside the repository. The link is read from its stdout and must be an address of `127.0.0.1`. `stop()` sends `SIGTERM` to the process group and requires the exit code 0 after that signal; if the server ended by itself before `stop()`, `stop()` fails whatever the exit code; a server that wrote into its home folder fails `stop()` with `STAND_HOME_WRITTEN` (decisions/0109). The server and its home folder are removed on a failure, on a signal, and when the runner stops a hung file.
